title: No element holds the award, the payment due date, the payment received-at time or the five-day term
source: TSD S5 T3.1 asset and asset_sale; TSD S5 T3.2 lists; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47, R-DIS-48 and R-DIS-49; FSD S5 A2.18; legacy RWB-E4-027 Data
description: R-DIS-47 starts the five-day payment term on AWARD_MADE, R-DIS-48 is conditioned on payment_received_at at or before payment_due_date, and R-DIS-49 on payment absent and payment_due_date passed. asset_sale of TSD S5 T3.1 carries id, asset_id, listing_id, contract_date, sale_date, sale_price, transfer_fee, specific_business_tax, corporate_income_tax, gain_loss and incentive_amount only, and listing and asset carry no term element. No source names a column, a table or a reference row for the award, its payment due date, the payment received-at time, the buyer of the award or the length of the term.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019; TSD S5 T3.2 LOV-HOLDING and LOV-LISTING; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-49 rows; legacy RWB-E4-027 Data table and legacy v_ace_npa_sale read.
proposed: Hold the award, the due date and the received-at time against the asset_sale record and the term length as versioned reference data, add no column in this story, and leave the buyer and the term as placeholders of this service until the LDM or the DB story names the elements.

title: The five-day term's rules R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50 sit across this story and RWB-S5-E4024-APP, and no source splits them
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50; FSD S5 A2.15 and A2.18; RWB-S5-E4024-APP s1 and s8; legacy RWB-E4-024 AC2 and RWB-E4-027 AC1
section: s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 Business rules; s9 State transitions
description: R-DIS-49 (cancel the award, score the vendor and reopen the round) and R-DIS-50 (reopen the round at the same price step) are claimed by RWB-S5-E4024-APP, and R-DIS-47 (start the five-day payment term) and R-DIS-48 (confirm the sale and start the title transfer) belong to FEAT-AST-18 and this story. No source says which story owns the expiry detection, the record of the cancellation and the write of the reopened round, so the same four rows are cited by two builds of one wave.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50; RWB-S5-E4024-APP s1 (it owns the award cancellation and the reopen) and s8 note; legacy RWB-E4-027 AC1 'releases the asset if it is missed'.
proposed: Keep each rule row single in rwb-decision; this story owns the term start and the payment confirmation (R-DIS-47, R-DIS-48) and raises the expiry signal, and RWB-S5-E4024-APP owns the cancellation, the vendor score and the reopen (R-DIS-49, R-DIS-50), so no rule is evaluated twice.

title: Legacy AC2, AC3 and the FSD A2.18 rule list name R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37, rules of the work order and the auction round, not the payment term
source: Legacy RWB-E4-027 AC2 and AC3; FSD S5 A2.18.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37; FSD S5 A2.7 and A2.15
section: s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 Business rules
description: The feature is the five-day payment term, yet its FSD rule list and its legacy criteria carry R-DIS-11 (WORK_ORDER_OPEN, WORK_ACCEPTED, release the invoice for payment and return the asset to hold, ASSET_HELD) and R-DIS-37 (ROUND_OPEN, BID_PLACED, record the bid against the round and the asset, BID_RECEIVED). R-DIS-11 is the work-order acceptance of the held-property feature and R-DIS-37 is the bid record of the auction-round feature (FEAT-AST-15), which RWB-S5-E4024-APP already builds. The term's own rules R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50 appear in no legacy criterion.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-027 acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3; FSD S5 A2.18.3.1 rule table rows R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37; FSD S5 A2.15.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37.
proposed: Keep AC2 and AC3 word for word and evaluate the two rules as the state gates they name, declare them once for the service, and let AC1 carry the term; the duplication with FEAT-AST-15 is recorded for the story-split review rather than resolved here.

title: No requirement row names the five-day payment term
source: FSD S5 Requirements served REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010; FSD S5 A2.18; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-AST-18; TSD S5 T8
description: FSD S5 serves ten requirements, and none of them names the five-day payment term, the payment confirmation or the release of an asset whose term was missed: REQ-S5-006 covers the price ladder and the re-list, REQ-S5-007 the second signature, REQ-S5-008 the title transfer and REQ-S5-009 the proceeds. The split plan carries an empty requirement list for this story, so no requirement id can be cited.
evidence: FSD S5 'Requirements served' table; TSD S5 T8 rows REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010; split plan slice RWB-S5-E4027-APP reqs empty.
proposed: Trace this story to FEAT-AST-18 of FSD S5 A2.18 and to the epic BRD row for that feature, and let the requirement register close the omission when the BRD of Epic 4 is baselined.

title: The consumed rows and the rwb-payment event carry no published name
source: Architecture v5 slide 13 (S5 listens to P8); TSD S5 T5.2 and T5.3; TSD P8; API Specification v4; TSD S5 T-A.1
section: s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: This story consumes the case state, the case-move answer and the payment fact of rwb-payment, and Architecture v5 slide 13 marks the S5 row and the P8 column as 'listens to events'. No source publishes the operation name of the case-move answer, the name or parameters of the payment fact activity, or the event name and payload of the payment event that carries a confirmed payment to this service; the topic is fixed by the naming rule as rwb.payment.events.v1 and the event name is not.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 connection matrix, row S5 Asset, columns P3, P8 and S9; TSD S5 T5.2; TSD S5 T5.3 (only AssetTakenOn published); API Specification v4 has no payment-event schema.
proposed: Declare the three consumed rows and the one event row in the contract baseline of RWB-S5-E4027-CON with the placeholder and its gap identifier, build against their fakes on Day 1, and adopt the owner's names at the tag without changing the behaviour.

title: DP-04 sits outside the declared pattern set while the DISPOSAL package must still be evaluated
source: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-04; split plan slice RWB-S5-E4027-APP patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; TSD S5 T4; Architecture v5 slide 12
section: s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules; s13 Solution plan
description: The story evaluates six DISPOSAL rules that only rwb-decision governs, which is the DP-04 marker (RuleEvaluator, Drools; H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON). The split plan lists DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only, so the platform contract row of DP-04 cannot be claimed here even though the rule package must be loaded and its version recorded.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 row DP-04; split plan slice patterns; TSD S5 T4 (DISPOSAL, 72 rules over 40 states); Architecture v5 slide 12 (Drools inside L4 activities, rule models governed in rwb-decision).
proposed: Load the DISPOSAL package and its version through the service template and reference it as rwb-decision's, add no platform dependency row to this story, and leave the DP-04 rows for the decision stories of the service.
